sentences.show: It flew into space and landed itself, with nobody on board. Years later, its own hangar fell on it.
This is Buran, the Soviet space shuttle.
On this day in 1988, it made its first and only flight.
Built to answer America's Space Shuttle, it took more than 1,000 companies.
A giant Energia rocket lifted it into orbit, without a single cosmonaut on board.
206 minutes later, its computer landed it, in a strong crosswind.
It stopped within 3 metres of its centre line.
On approach, the computer even chose a turn that engineers had rated at just 3%.
Then the Soviet Union collapsed, and in 1993, Buran was cancelled.
In 2002, its hangar roof at Baikonur fell in, destroying Buran, and killing at least six workers.
Also on this day: Sherman began his March to the Sea, and the first Xbox went on sale.
